rubric.evidence: evidence/preflight-browser.log records Transformers.js 3.7.5 loading canonical revision 7e3ba62ce16b379a1ab479346b66f192e76f51b7 and exactly 605,804,513 ONNX bytes, then real WASM inference: sneaker top=a white sneaker 0.999817 (332 ms); shirt top=a sports t-shirt 0.999728 (276 ms). evidence/acceptance.json then runs real local inference on desktop and mobile for all 8 family routes.
rubric.notes: All heavy inference and tensor post-processing run in a dedicated module Web Worker.

rubric.evidence: All 16 light-theme route/device runs produced 4 label rows and 4 tensor rows. The UI exposes real image/text projection dimensions, per-label cosine, scaled logit and relative softmax score; the multi-model route exposes 4 results from each genuine model.
rubric.notes: Scores are explicitly described as relative to the supplied label set, not calibrated facts.

rubric.evidence: Page, catalogue, loader and worker agree on patrickjohncyh/fashion-clip, immutable revision 7e3ba62ce16b379a1ab479346b66f192e76f51b7, fp32, WASM, MIT, onnx/model.onnx and 605,804,513 bytes. The second stage is independently pinned to Xenova/clip-vit-base-patch16 revision 342fdf2f67aded64d138ff074745fb4a5d2bba5f; its q8 ONNX is exactly 152,040,303 bytes with SHA-256 cf5b03d7c03cd78498b0d59a905552b549ae91af4e99ffb985103aa9424d2272.
rubric.notes: The multi-model page states both exact artifacts and the 757,844,816-byte combined ONNX total.

rubric.evidence: Every stage uses createModelLoader with an immutable revision cache key. scripts/produce-fashion-clip-evidence.mjs reproducibly exercises first-visit absent/download, progress, current cached auto-init, partial/evicted, visible error/retry, release/re-init, offline cached, and clear states; immutable stale/update, byte-corruption and WebGPU-unsupported states are retained as explicit not-applicable rows with architecture-specific reasons.
rubric.notes: Shared model-cache, progress adapter, retry, clear-cache and memory diagnostics are exercised in the browser rather than inferred from retained prose.

rubric.evidence: The committed producer records observable shared checking/download-required/downloading/initialising/ready/partial/error/retry/released/clear/offline states for both stages, including the deliberately blocked request that creates the visible retry path. Every request receives a terminal response/byte record or is the one expected blocked failure; all unexpected failures fail the run.
rubric.notes: Immutable stale/update is not applicable, Cache Storage cannot retain partial response bodies so byte-corrupt is not a separately observable loader state, and requiresWebGPU=false makes the WebGPU-unsupported branch not applicable; these are explicit N/A evidence, never passes.

rubric.evidence: For every route on desktop and mobile, the producer changes both native sample buttons with Space/Enter, focuses and changes the file input with a different real fixture, edits the textarea through CDP key events, keyboard-activates Reset, edits again, and keyboard-activates Rank. It keyboard-drives shared Download, file-details disclosure, Release/re-init, Retry and Clear controls across both stages.
rubric.notes: The two-stage route exposes and independently drives both pinned shared loaders. Native file-picker chrome is unavailable to headless CDP, so DOM.setFileInputFiles is retained as the honest browser-protocol equivalent while focus/value/change are asserted.

rubric.evidence: Result DOM is empty until the worker returns real tensor-derived output. Retained outputs discriminate both fixtures and change across route vocabularies; no result array or fallback ranking is embedded in source.

The regenerated 32-cell evidence reports zero unnamed buttons and zero images missing alt, plus per-control focus/input method/value-before/value-after records. Native labels, buttons, textarea, file input, disclosure summary, aria-pressed samples, role=meter score bars, live status and semantic tables are checked in the browser.
rubric.notes: Licensed fixture credit is injected visibly by the shared image-credit annotator.

rubric.evidence: evidence/acceptance.json retains 32/32 screenshots for 8 routes × desktop/mobile × light/dark. Every driven mobile cell reports no horizontal overflow after the file-input fix; flexible intrinsic grids and wrapped actions keep controls usable at 360×740.
rubric.notes: The page honestly warns that 578 MiB download and ~1.2 GiB initialization memory can exceed mobile tab/storage limits.

rubric.evidence: worker.js performs image preprocessing, tokenization, the ONNX forward pass and cosine/softmax loops off-main-thread. The main thread only updates bounded DOM rows. Screenshots use explicit image dimensions; below-fold fixture is lazy-loaded.
rubric.notes: The canonical fp32 export is large by upstream fact; the UX gates its download and discloses the cost rather than hiding it.

guidanceConsulted.query: large in-browser image embedding model responsive accessible download controls off-main-thread inference
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Separate UI updates from heavy computation, offload >250 ms work to a Web Worker, preserve explicit image dimensions and avoid automatic large transfers.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: all preprocessing/inference/post-processing is worker-owned; the absent 578 MiB model requires explicit Download; fixture dimensions are declared.

guidanceConsulted.query: large in-browser image embedding model responsive accessible download controls off-main-thread inference
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Move work exceeding a frame budget off the main thread; use scheduler.yield fallback only for unavoidable main-thread loops.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied by eliminating heavy main-thread loops: tensor math stays in worker.js and DOM rendering is four bounded rows.

guidanceConsulted.query: large in-browser image embedding model responsive accessible download controls off-main-thread inference
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic landmarks/headings/native labelled controls, explicit image dimensions, accessible names and live status.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied across overview and ladder pages with main/header/section/footer, sequential headings, native labels/buttons/file input, role=status and role=meter.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow for file input and long model identifiers
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsic grids, min-inline-size:0 on shrinkable children, wrapping flex rows and explicit max inline sizes for intrinsic controls.

guidanceConsulted.evidence: fashion.css; final acceptance mobile overflow=false on every route

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible keyboard control validation loading progress error retry offline cache states responsive browser evidence
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native controls, prove actual focus and keyboard operation, keep status/error feedback perceivable, and do not substitute a checklist for interaction testing.

openQuestions: Mobile layouts are verified on a headless emulated 360×740 device; physical low-memory mobile hardware may still terminate a 1.2 GiB WASM initialization, which the UI discloses rather than claiming support without qualification.

followUpGoals.goal: Measure physical-device peak memory across representative Android/iOS browsers and refine the existing mobile requirement disclosure without changing route identity.

summary: Canonical FashionCLIP 2.0 family with exact pinned primary lineage and an independently pinned 152,040,303-byte general-CLIP q8 stage, 8 unchanged routes, genuine worker inference, shared lifecycle, visible tensors and rights-safe apparel fixtures. The bound acceptance is produced by a committed fail-closed browser driver rather than trusted retained prose.
